task_instruction: Rewrite each sentence in the passive voice. Change the verb in the subordinate clause and keep the main clause unchanged.
paragraphs: In the late Middle Ages, a royal historian records events at a stone castle. {{red:The steward explains that the masons built the outer wall after the northern raid.}} {{mask_1}} {{red:The reeve believes that the villagers have repaired the wooden bridge before the winter thaw.}} {{mask_2}} {{red:The castle captain reports that a messenger carried the duke's sealed letter through the eastern gate.}} {{mask_3}} {{red:The chronicler notes that the royal clerk is copying the treaty into the archive book.}} {{mask_4}}

As preparations begin for a diplomatic visit, the steward checks the guest rooms. {{red:He says that the servants are preparing the great hall for the visiting envoy.}} {{mask_5}} {{red:The marshal expects that the blacksmith will mend the damaged gate hinge by dawn.}} {{mask_6}} {{red:The abbess remembers that the prior had stored the monastery's grain accounts in a locked chest.}} {{mask_7}} {{red:The council knows that the royal seal can authenticate the duke's orders.}} {{mask_8}}

The envoy arrives with a party from a neighboring territory. {{red:The herald announces that the duke has sent a delegation to discuss the border.}} {{mask_9}} {{red:The captain observes that the guards are escorting the visitors across the courtyard.}} {{mask_10}} {{red:The steward discovers that someone has removed a page from the guest register.}} {{mask_11}} {{red:The chronicler writes that the queen will receive the envoy after the council meets.}} {{mask_12}}

During the council, the nobles consider the terms of a trade agreement. {{red:The chancellor insists that the scribes must record every change to the treaty.}} {{mask_13}} {{red:The envoy admits that his messenger misplaced one of the boundary maps.}} {{mask_14}} {{red:The reeve explains that the villagers were rebuilding the mill when the river rose.}} {{mask_15}} {{red:The abbess says that the monastery has offered the travelers shelter for the night.}} {{mask_16}}

Before the delegation departs, the royal household prepares gifts and copies of the agreement. {{red:The steward confirms that the treasurer has counted the silver coins.}} {{mask_17}} {{red:The captain believes that the guards will protect the bridge until the envoys leave.}} {{mask_18}} {{red:The chronicler hopes that future scholars may preserve the treaty in the royal archive.}} {{mask_19}} {{red:The queen requests that the council review the final document before it is sealed.}} {{mask_20}} The historian finishes the account, noting how careful records helped the two territories avoid another dispute.
